title: The Absolute Effect - Master Trial Roster
rules: One entry represents one underlying trial/study, not one publication.
Trial aliases, acronyms, registry names and follow-up publications are collapsed into the same entry.
A trial-page entry counts as uploaded evidence.
A unique Trial-of-the-Day archived in data/trial-archive.json counts even if no permanent trial page exists.
Daily proposal files are not added merely because a trial was proposed; they must correspond to an uploaded trial page or archived Trial-of-the-Day to enter this roster.
Before future selection, this roster must be checked together with current Trial-of-the-Day and archive data.
After an approved daily batch is uploaded, the roster is updated the same day before subsequent daily selection.

Daily selection must avoid not only duplicate trials/studies but also consecutive trials that answer essentially the same clinical question; selection should maximize distinct clinical questions unless replication/evolution is deliberate.

Every trial page must remain visually informative when neither NNT nor NNH can be defensibly calculated: show a chart/pictogram of the strongest reported outcome (e.g. survival, response, progression, toxicity, or relative effect) using source-reported values only; label endpoint and time horizon; never derive NNT from median survival.

Every permanent trial page must distinguish historical trial results from current practice context. Audit for later follow-up publications, meta-analyses, guideline changes, and whether the intervention remains standard; display a dated current-practice context and linked sources. Do not overwrite original trial results with newer recommendations.

Do not mark a trial clinically current based only on its original publication date or presence of a source link. A freshness review must check subsequent follow-up, later practice-changing trials/meta-analyses, current disease-specific guideline recommendations, and whether the intervention remains standard; record dated sources and review status.

Every rostered and newly added trial page must be checked for an actual, readable outcome visualization: show a defensible NNT/NNH patient pictogram when possible; otherwise chart a source-reported survival, response, recurrence, toxicity, or relative-effect endpoint. Pages with no detectable numeric endpoint must be explicitly flagged for manual review rather than silently left as abstract-only. Never derive NNT from median survival.
Use a small shared set of treatment-setting categories across tumour sites; preserve the original specific setting in setting_detail and the full clinical question.

A batch is not releasable unless the latest-batch release validator passes: exact roster/page identity, canonical primary DOI link, no non-finite chart widths, no generic trial headings, no duplicated sections, and no conflicting NNT claims.

For every NNT/NNH pictogram, store the endpoint, time horizon, source-reported absolute percentage-point difference, and NNT/NNH in a structured absolute_effect object. data-benefit/data-harm must contain the absolute percentage-point differences, never 100 divided by NNT/NNH.
Do not calculate or display NNT from non-comparative trials, including randomized studies with an internal-control arm; display the source-reported outcome rates and state why NNT is not appropriate.

For randomized non-comparative designs with an internal control, show the arm-specific source-reported outcome rates as descriptive data; do not label the difference as absolute treatment benefit or render an NNT/NNH pictogram.

Any numeric NNT/NNH appearing anywhere on a trial page must be represented in absolute_effect with the exact endpoint and time horizon; pictogram values must equal the absolute percentage-point difference, not 100 divided by NNT/NNH.

Taxonomy: primary setting represents the treatment context, not disease extent. Relapsed / Refractory takes precedence when trial eligibility requires recurrence, progression on/after prior systemic therapy, or established treatment resistance. Advanced / Metastatic is reserved for advanced disease without a defining prior-progression/resistance requirement, including first-line treatment and maintenance in non-progressive disease.

Record disease extent, prior-treatment status, and treatment line as separate dimensions where supported by trial eligibility. A trial may be metastatic and relapsed/refractory simultaneously; do not duplicate the trial or force metastatic disease extent into the primary setting.

NSCLC-specific primary-setting taxonomy: use only Early, Metastatic, Adjuvant, Neoadjuvant, or Consolidation. Do not use Relapsed / Refractory, Advanced / Metastatic, Locally Advanced, Perioperative, or other primary-setting labels for NSCLC. Classify previously treated/progressed advanced NSCLC as Metastatic and retain relapse/progression/prior-line context in separate metadata or setting_detail. Use Neoadjuvant for perioperative trials whose treatment begins preoperatively; use Consolidation for post-definitive CRT systemic therapy; use Early for localized/locally advanced non-metastatic definitive-treatment trials.
